title: GENIE - Genetic Information and Education_Study 2
summary: Rare genetic disorders often manifest as early as childhood and present affected families with many new questions and uncertainties. Especially following a diagnosis, it is important to convey medical information in an understandable way so that patients and their families can better understand the condition and cope with the challenges it presents. The GENIE (Genetic Information and Education) research project investigates how information can be conveyed in a clear and patient-centered manner during human genetic counseling. The project consists of two sub-studies. The second sub-study examines informational videos on Noonan syndrome and Kabuki syndrome. Parents and family members of children with one of these diagnoses are eligible to participate. Following their regular human genetic counseling session, participants will watch an informational video about the respective condition. The videos are available in German, English, and Arabic and provide key information about the condition, possible treatments, daily life with the diagnosis, and additional support services. Before and after watching the video, participants will complete an online questionnaire. Among other things, the study will examine how clear and helpful the videos are, how well the information presented is understood, and how much participants trust the information provided. In addition, participants can voluntarily take part in an interview about four to six weeks later. During the interview, they will be asked how helpful the videos were in retrospect and whether they have any further needs for information or support. The goal of the project is to better tailor genetic counseling to the needs of patients and their families and to assess whether accessible, digital, and multilingual information resources can effectively complement in-person counseling.

None
